newsitem.title: UK: UK Referendum Party launches poster campaign.
newsitem.headline: UK Referendum Party launches poster campaign.

text.p: Britain's new Referendum Party launched a nationwide poster campaign on Saturday calling for people to be given a chance to decide on the nation's future in the European Union.

The roadside billboard posters, strong on anti-EU rhetoric, demand a "proper referendum" on Europe and will be shown on some 4,500 sites around the country in a bid to sway Britons to vote for the Referendum Party in national elections due by May.
Carrying the slogan "Brussels Spouts", one poster claims: "Every week Brussels issues over 100 new rules that we must obey".
Another says; "Why not John? Why can't we have a proper referendum on Europe Mr Major?"

The Referendum Party, formed last year by millionaire businessman Sir James Goldsmith, has vowed to put up candidates in more than 100 seats and is seen by political analysts as a serious threat to Prime Minister John Major's Conservative Party.
Major is already some 20 points behind the main opposition Labour Party and even a few hundred votes for a Referendum Party candidate could deny his Conservatives vital parliamentary places.
The Referendum Party is vague on the precise question which should be put to the people and says that it will disband once a plebiscite has been held.
The Party has taken out newspaper advertisements alleging that politicians took Britain into a federal European superstate "by deceit" and hid warnings about the powers to be handed over to Brussels.

It cites a 1960 letter written by then Lord Chancellor, Lord Kilmuir, saying that joining the EU would involve "serious" losses of sovereignty. Britain joined the European Union in 1972 after a referendum.
